stem: in Surah Al-A'raf (7:11–12), God asks Iblis what kept him from bowing to Adam when commanded. what reason does Iblis give?
options: Adam would shed blood and spread harm on earth
he was created of fire, and Adam only of clay
Adam had already eaten from the forbidden tree
he had been told to bow to God and none other
why: Qur'an 7:12 (Pickthall): "I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud." The worry about bloodshed is the angels' question in 2:30, and the tree comes later in the story.

es.stem: en la sura Al-A'raf (7:11–12), Dios le pregunta a Iblís qué le impidió inclinarse ante Adán cuando se le ordenó. ¿qué razón da Iblís?
options: Adán derramaría sangre y sembraría daño en la tierra
él fue creado de fuego, y Adán solo de barro
Adán ya había comido del árbol prohibido
le habían dicho que se inclinara solo ante Dios
es.why: Corán 7:12: "Yo soy mejor que él. A mí me creaste de fuego, y a él lo creaste de barro". La preocupación por el derramamiento de sangre es la pregunta de los ángeles en 2:30, y el árbol llega más tarde en el relato.

stem: in Surah Al-A'raf, both Iblis and Adam fall into disobedience. how does Adam's response (7:23) differ from Iblis's (7:16)?
options: Adam blames the whisperer; Iblis admits his own pride
Adam blames his wife; Iblis admits he has done wrong
Adam asks to stay in the garden; Iblis asks for pardon
Adam owns his wrong; Iblis says God sent him astray
why: Qur'an 7:23: Adam and his wife say "Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves." In 7:16 Iblis says "Now, because Thou hast sent me astray...". Iblis asks only for respite (7:14), never forgiveness; 2:37 says God relented toward Adam.

es.stem: en la sura Al-A'raf, tanto Iblís como Adán caen en la desobediencia. ¿en qué se diferencia la respuesta de Adán (7:23) de la de Iblís (7:16)?
options: Adán culpa al que susurra; Iblís admite su propio orgullo
Adán culpa a su esposa; Iblís admite que hizo mal
Adán pide quedarse en el jardín; Iblís pide perdón
Adán reconoce su falta; Iblís dice que Dios lo extravió
es.why: Corán 7:23: Adán y su esposa dicen "¡Señor nuestro! Hemos sido injustos con nosotros mismos". En 7:16 Iblís dice "Porque Tú me has extraviado...". Iblís solo pide una prórroga (7:14), nunca perdón; 2:37 dice que Dios aceptó el arrepentimiento de Adán.

stem: in Surah Al-An'am (6:76–78), Ibrahim turns from the star, the moon and the sun, saying "I love not things that set." by that same test, why would he refuse to take a great river as his lord?
options: a river is shaped by the hands of the people
a river lies far lower than the stars and sun
a river can run dry and vanish like the rest
a river was not among his people's idols
why: Qur'an 6:76–79: each light is rejected because it sets (afilin: things that fade and vanish), and Ibrahim turns to the One who created the heavens and the earth. Anything that can pass away fails the same test.

es.stem: en la sura Al-An'am (6:76–78), Ibrahim se aparta de la estrella, la luna y el sol, diciendo "no amo lo que se pone". con esa misma prueba, ¿por qué se negaría a tomar un gran río como su señor?
options: un río lo moldean las manos de la gente
un río está mucho más abajo que el sol y los astros
un río puede secarse y desaparecer como los demás
un río no estaba entre los ídolos de su pueblo
es.why: Corán 6:76–79: cada luz es rechazada porque se pone (afilin: lo que se desvanece y desaparece), e Ibrahim se vuelve hacia Quien creó los cielos y la tierra. Todo lo que puede pasar no supera la misma prueba.

stem: in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:62–66), asked who smashed the town's idols, Ibrahim points to the largest and says "question them, if they can speak." what is he leading the people to see?
options: idols that cannot speak can neither help nor harm
the chief idol had turned in anger on the others
the idols must first be judged by the town elders
the largest idol alone deserved their worship
why: Qur'an 21:65–66: the people admit "Well thou knowest that these speak not," and Ibrahim asks whether they worship, instead of Allah, what can neither profit nor harm them. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari counts his words as said for Allah's sake.

es.stem: en la sura Al-Anbiya (21:62–66), cuando le preguntan quién destrozó los ídolos del pueblo, Ibrahim señala el más grande y dice "pregúntenles, si es que pueden hablar". ¿qué quiere que la gente vea?
options: ídolos que no hablan no pueden ayudar ni dañar
el ídolo mayor se había enojado con los demás
los ancianos del pueblo debían juzgar a los ídolos
solo el ídolo más grande merecía su adoración
es.why: Corán 21:65–66: la gente admite "Bien sabes que estos no hablan", e Ibrahim pregunta si adoran, en lugar de Allah, lo que no puede beneficiarlos ni dañarlos. Un hadiz de Sahih al-Bujari cuenta sus palabras como dichas por causa de Allah.

stem: in Surah Yusuf (12:89–92), when his brothers finally recognize Yusuf in Egypt and admit they were wrong, how does he answer them?
options: he tells them God will settle their account in the end
he forgives them once their father has pardoned them
he says no blame is on them today and prays for them
he keeps their grain until they repay what they took
why: Qur'an 12:92 (Pickthall): "Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy." (la tathriba 'alaykumu l-yawm: no reproach on you today).

es.stem: en la sura Yusuf (12:89–92), cuando sus hermanos por fin reconocen a Yusuf en Egipto y admiten que obraron mal, ¿cómo les responde?
options: les dice que Dios les pedirá cuentas al final
los perdona cuando su padre ya los haya perdonado
les dice que hoy no hay reproche y ruega por ellos
retiene su grano hasta que paguen lo que tomaron
es.why: Corán 12:92: "Hoy no hay reproche contra ustedes. Que Allah los perdone; Él es el más Misericordioso de los misericordiosos" (la tazriba 'alaykumu l-yawm: hoy no hay reproche contra ustedes).

stem: in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:87), Yunus (Dhu'n-Nun, "the man of the fish") cries out from within the darkness. what does he say?
options: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; have mercy on us
There is no god but You; glory to You; I was wrong
My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send me
My Lord, open my breast for me and ease my task
why: Qur'an 21:87 (Pickthall): "There is no God save Thee. Be Thou glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer." The others are Adam and his wife (7:23) and Musa (28:24; 20:25–26). A hadith in Tirmidhi calls this the prayer of Dhu'n-Nun.

es.stem: en la sura Al-Anbiya (21:87), Yunus (Dhu'n-Nun, "el del pez") clama desde la oscuridad. ¿qué dice?
options: Señor nuestro, fuimos injustos con nosotros; ten piedad
No hay dios sino Tú; gloria a Ti; yo obré mal
Señor mío, necesito el bien que me hagas descender
Señor mío, ensancha mi pecho y facilita mi tarea
es.why: Corán 21:87: "No hay dios sino Tú. ¡Glorificado seas! Ciertamente he sido de los injustos". Las demás son de Adán y su esposa (7:23) y de Musa (28:24; 20:25–26). Un hadiz de Tirmidhi la llama la súplica de Dhu'n-Nun.

stem: In Ibn Ishaq's life of the Prophet, the clans of Quraysh nearly fight over who will set the Black Stone back in the rebuilt Ka'ba. How does the young Muhammad ﷺ settle it?
why: Chosen as the first man through the sanctuary gate, al-Amin spreads a cloak, lays the Black Stone on it, and has a leader from each clan hold its edges and lift it together; then he sets the stone in place with his own hand. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Ibn Hisham)

rubric.point: Says he places the stone on a cloak or cloth and has the leaders of the clans hold it and lift it together. Saying only that he 'made peace' or 'decided fairly' does not count.
Says the point is that every clan shares the honor, so no single clan wins and the fight is avoided. Mentioning only that they lifted it together, without the shared honor, counts as partly.
Mentions that he was chosen because he was the next man through the gate, or that they trusted him as al-Amin, or that he set the stone in the wall himself (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En la vida del Profeta de Ibn Ishaq, los clanes de Quraysh casi pelean por quién volverá a colocar la Piedra Negra en la Kaaba reconstruida. ¿Cómo lo resuelve el joven Muhammad ﷺ?
es.why: Elegido por ser el primero en entrar por la puerta del santuario, al-Amin extiende un manto, pone en él la Piedra Negra y hace que un jefe de cada clan tome sus bordes para levantarla juntos; luego él mismo coloca la piedra en su lugar. Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah.

stem: When early Muslims took refuge in Abyssinia and Quraysh sent envoys asking the Najashi (the Negus) to hand them back, what did the king do, and what did Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recite before him?
why: The Najashi refused to hand over the refugees before hearing them; Ja'far described what the Prophet ﷺ taught and recited the opening of Surah Maryam; the king wept and let the Muslims stay under his protection. Umm Salamah's account, in Ibn Ishaq and the Musnad of Ahmad.
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah; Musnad Ahmad (Umm Salamah's account)

rubric.point: Says the king refused to hand the Muslims over and let them stay under his protection. Saying only that he 'was kind to them' counts as partly.
Names Surah Maryam (or the passage on Zakariyya, Maryam and the birth of 'Isa) as what Ja'far recited. Saying only 'the Qur'an' counts as partly.
Mentions that the king insisted on hearing the Muslims first, or that he and his bishops wept at the recitation (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Cuando los primeros musulmanes se refugiaron en Abisinia y Quraysh envió emisarios para pedirle al Nayashi (el Negus) que los devolviera, ¿qué hizo el rey y qué recitó Ya'far ibn Abi Talib ante él?
es.why: El Nayashi se negó a entregar a los refugiados sin antes escucharlos; Ya'far describió lo que enseñaba el Profeta ﷺ y recitó el comienzo de la sura Maryam; el rey lloró y dejó que los musulmanes se quedaran bajo su protección. Relato de Umm Salamah, en Ibn Ishaq y el Musnad de Ahmad.
